channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: FRAME/SEQUENCE Issue 4 — On the Destruction of Art
item.description: FRAME/SEQUENCE is a Philadelphia print periodical founded in 2025 by photographer and educator Lily Colman (RISD MFA, 2020) as a publishing non-profit under the fiscal sponsorship of CultureWorks of Philadelphia, spotlighting underrepresented and emerging photographers, writers, artists and communities across Philadelphia and Greater Pennsylvania. Issue 4, due out as the March 2027 periodical, takes the theme "On the Destruction of Art": what it means to make work in an age of cultural and societal destruction, how artists keep working in those conditions, and how a society responds when art itself is debased, degraded or commodified. The editors want work that uses destruction or ephemerality as method — rupture and renewal — alongside writing that reads art's place in culture through an art-historical or contemporary lens, and they say explicitly that they are looking for everything from photographers working on the ground in real time to more interpretive photographic and written responses. The regional frame is relaxed for this issue: the periodical still focuses on Philadelphia, but submissions for Issue 4 are open to any artist or writer, and former University of the Arts students forced to transfer when that school closed, along with their professors, are especially encouraged. Photography, creative writing (poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction), visual art, mixed media and community-focused projects are accepted, and all visual art must incorporate photography in some way. Submit between five and ten images per edition as JPEG or PNG through the Airtable form, each file under 10 MB, 240 dpi acceptable and 300 dpi preferred for print; previously published work is eligible as long as you retain the right to republish, noted in the submission. The application fee is $25 for new applicants and non-members of Da Vinci Art Alliance and free both for DVAA members and for anyone featured in any earlier edition, covering up to five submissions. Accepted contributors are paid a one-time cash award per accepted piece plus a royalty apportioned by level of contribution out of a shared royalty pool paid through the fiscal sponsor; artists keep full ownership and all rights and may keep using, selling or publishing the work, signing a publishing agreement by DocuSign if selected. Three inconsistencies sit on the organiser's own pages, and one of them is about money. The submissions FAQ still answers the deadline question with the inaugural issue's window (June 20 – July 18, 2025), while the dated Issue 4 block on both the submissions page and the homepage reads September 15 – November 15, 2026. The About page says twice that the periodical charges nothing to submit — "we do not charge a submission fee, and we pay our artists for having their work published" and "submissions are always free" — and the live Issue 4 Airtable form carries no payment step, no fee line and no membership question, while the FAQ's $25 sentence is reproduced word for word from the previous edition's submissions page and names no way to pay; budget for the $25, but it may never be collected. And the team page calls the periodical quarterly where the homepage and submissions page call it semiannual. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $25 (free for DVAA members and previously featured artists). Prize: Publication + cash award per accepted piece.

item.title: Collected Light · Photosynthesis NZ
item.description: Open call for "all art made with light" from Photosynthesis, a fully volunteer-run non-profit in Ōtautahi Christchurch that operates the only gallery in the city dedicated to photography, alongside a community darkroom, studio and digital workspaces for hire. Collected Light is the second edition of a regular mega group show: the first, Open 2026, ran in February and March 2026 with more than 80 artists and over 180 pieces, and the organisers describe the format as "a cross-section of the state-of-our-arts". Artists of all ages and experience levels may enter one to three still works made with light — photographs, prints, photo books and zines are all named. Each entry needs a title, a short description, an image and a display plan. There is no size limit, but you must give the finished outside height and width in millimetres including any frame or mount (and the depth if it matters), measured as planned if the work is not yet printed; later changes need the gallery's approval so it can plan the layout. A panel reviews every entry after submissions close and selects the show; the organisers say they cannot include every entry but hope to include at least one submission per artist. Work may be offered for sale with a koha commission of 20% to Photosynthesis on any sale. Print workshops run through November for anyone who needs help producing their piece. Installation begins 28 November and the show opens on 4 December 2026 at the Photosynthesis gallery on Battersea Street in Sydenham; the call page says the exhibition end date is still to be confirmed, but the gallery’s own exhibitions calendar already dates the run 4–20 December 2026. Selection, delivery and collection dates and the opening time are still to be announced. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Pedantic Arts Residency 2027
item.description: Four-week residency on Penn Avenue in Pittsburgh's Garfield arts corridor, run by Pedantic Arts (a Casey Droege Cultural Productions programme now becoming a standalone non-profit). Each cohort is three creatives in three distinct roles — a visual artist, an organiser/curator and a writer — and the programme is built around exchange and study rather than output: it asks for no final deliverable and states that it "prioritizes immersion over production". The visual-artist role is defined broadly as "anyone working in a creative field of the Fine Arts be it painting, craft, performance art, social practice, etc." The call names no medium at all, but Pedantic’s own cohort archive does: its June 2023 cohort page describes that cohort’s visual artist, Akea Brionne, as "a Creole visual artist based in Detroit, MI whose work sits at the intersection of photography, textiles, and moving image", and carries Cranbrook’s May 2026 announcement of her first solo museum exhibition under the headline "Photography Alumna Akea Brionne". Residents get a private bedroom and desk in a newly built three-bedroom apartment (shared kitchen, living space, laundry, outdoor space and street parking; one bedroom and bathroom are ADA-compliant and the building has a lift), a $2,000 stipend paid half on arrival and half on completion, facilitated access to Pittsburgh's creative community, tickets and passes to local institutions, and a Pittsburgh-based guide working in a similar field who builds a schedule and opens up local contacts. Weekly programming includes private dinners, studio visits and museum tours, some public and some reserved for the cohort. Two terms are on offer in this call: Summer 2027, 5 June – 2 July 2027, and Fall 2027, 2 – 29 October 2027; you may apply for both but will be invited to only one. Applicants must be 18 or older and must live outside the greater Pittsburgh metropolitan area, which Pedantic defines as Allegheny, Armstrong, Beaver, Butler, Fayette, Washington and Westmoreland counties — Pittsburgh-based creatives are pointed to the Get Involved form instead. International applicants are welcome and Pedantic says it will support visa applications, while cautioning prospective residents to check their own country's travel position first; residents arrange and pay for their own travel to Pittsburgh. Applications were free through 28 September 2026 and cost $20 from 29 September, payable to Casey Droege Cultural Productions, until the open call closes on 15 October 2026 at 11:59pm EST. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: 4-week residency + $2,000 stipend.

item.title: I would like it to be · Grosse Pointe Artists Association
item.description: A juried show at the Grosse Pointe Artists Association's gallery on the War Memorial campus in Grosse Pointe Farms, on the Lake St Clair shore north-east of Detroit. The theme asks artists to share a dream or creative spark — to picture the world ahead for themselves and for others as they would like it to be. The juror is Sabrina Nelson, a Detroit artist of more than thirty-five years and a Kresge Artist Fellow, who teaches studio art at the Detroit Institute of Arts, where she lectures and gives artist demonstrations, and is on staff at the College for Creative Studies. First prize is a solo show at the gallery in 2027. The call is open to any artist over 18, plus alumni of the association's Promising Artists exhibitions — there is no geographic bar, but accepted work has to be in the gallery's hands for intake between noon and 2.30pm on Saturday 5 December, so travel or shipping arrangements are the artist's problem to solve. Work must be original: anything made under an instructor's direction, commercial kits, prefabricated models and hobby crafts are all ineligible, as are large installations and pieces already shown with the association. There is no size limit, though gallery space is a factor in final acceptance. Entry runs $30 for members and $40 for non-members for the first two pieces, with up to four more at $10 each and a $3 transaction fee on top; images must be JPGs of at least 600 × 600 pixels, evenly lit and free of reflections. Two-dimensional work should arrive framed and ready to hang, with acrylic rather than glass. Not everything has to be priced to sell, but anything that is and does carries a commission of 35% on member work and 45% on non-member work, so price accordingly. Entries close at midnight on Monday 16 November 2026, results are emailed by Friday 20 November, the exhibition runs 9 December 2026 to 22 January 2027 with a gallery talk at 2pm on Saturday 12 December, and work is collected between 10am and noon on Saturday 23 January. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $40 for 2 works ($30 members), $10 per extra work, +$3 transaction fee. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Flower & Fauna: A Botanical & Beings Exhibition · Avondale Arts Alliance
item.description: A themed winter show at the Avondale Arts Center, the volunteer-run gallery of the Avondale Arts Alliance just east of Atlanta in Avondale Estates. Every work must feature flowers, plants, animals or some combination of the three — the alliance states that anything outside that is disqualified automatically — and both traditional treatments and loose, creative interpretations are invited, with no restriction on medium beyond the subject rule. Entrants may submit one to six pieces in a single entry, one entry per artist, as JPG, PDF or PNG files up to 50MB each; the fee is $15 for three pieces and $30 for six, artists 18 and under enter free with a voucher code, and the alliance asks anyone for whom the fee is a hardship to email before submitting. The call is open only to artists in Atlanta and the surrounding area, because accepted work has to be hand delivered: drop-off is 10am to 2pm on Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November, the gallery does not accept shipped artwork, and a friend or family member may deliver on an artist's behalf. Status emails go out by midnight on Saturday 31 October. The exhibition opens with a 6–9pm reception on Saturday 14 November and closes with another on Saturday 19 December; attendance at neither is required. All work must be priced for sale with the alliance retaining 30% of any sale, and prices cannot be changed after acceptance, so the alliance asks artists to build the commission into the price before applying. Submissions close at 11.59pm on Friday 23 October 2026. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $15 for 3 works, $30 for 6. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals 2027–2028 · Alexander Brest Gallery
item.description: The Alexander Brest Gallery is the exhibition space of the Linda Berry Stein College of Arts & Sciences at Jacksonville University, on the university's riverfront campus across the St Johns River from downtown Jacksonville, and it programmes its season from an annual open call rather than from invitations alone. For the 2027–2028 season the gallery, under director Zakriya Rabani, is taking proposals for its 2,300 square foot space in 2D, 3D, installation and video work — photography sits inside the 2D remit, and the call is explicit that proposals are welcome from established and emerging artists in all mediums. Both solo and group exhibitions are considered, as are curatorial proposals, and a team may apply with one shared résumé of no more than a page per member. Applications are free and go in as a single PDF of no more than 50MB, named LastName_FirstName_ExhibitionTitle_Proposal.pdf, holding three things: an exhibition narrative that opens with a clear thesis statement (project proposals for unfinished or installation work also need a timeline, and any on-site making has to be installable in under three days); a CV of one to two pages per person with a preferred contact method; and an image list of up to 12 high-resolution images for a solo show or three per person for a group show, each image on its own page at large size with artist, title, medium, dimensions and year underneath. Video and audio work is submitted as streaming links plus stills, and an all-video application needs no image PDF at all. One requirement sets this call apart from a straight exhibition application: every proposal must include a student engagement activity at JU — a studio visit, a lecture, a tool or material demonstration, student participation in the exhibition narrative, or a collaboration with another college on campus. The gallery publishes its floor plan and installation photographs for applicants to plan against, and states that it is committed to showing artists across race, colour, creed, gender, gender variance, sexual orientation, national origin, age, religion, marital status, political affiliation and mental or physical disability. The call is open to artists anywhere in the continental United States and closes on 14 December 2026. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: NYC Open Call 2027–28 · apexart
item.description: apexart, the non-profit at 291 Church Street in Tribeca, runs its New York open call every October, and this round is for the 2027–28 exhibition season. You submit a 500-word proposal for a focused, idea-driven, original group exhibition of at least three artists working independently of one another — four if you are both the organiser and one of the artists. Nothing else goes in: no biographical statement, no CV, no links, no images, no name, because proposals are judged anonymously. The proposal text itself becomes the first half of the eventual exhibition essay. Selection is unusual and is the reason this call is worth the effort for anyone without a résumé: rather than a panel, a changing international jury of more than 600 people across 70 countries votes online each November, every juror sees at least fifty randomised proposals with the submitters' names hidden, and apexart states that proposals are judged on the strength of the exhibition idea and the organiser's ability to communicate it rather than on social connections or past accomplishments. Winning organisers get a $10,000 budget per exhibition: $8,000 to cover curator travel, artwork shipping, artist and public-programme honorariums, equipment and installation, plus an honorarium of up to $2,000 for coordinating the project and writing the brochure essay. apexart separately covers approved insurance, advertising, publicity, documentation, the design, printing and mailing of the exhibition brochure and the opening reception, and handles most of the logistics including loan agreements and shipping. Anyone from anywhere can apply at any experience level — trained and student curators, artists, writers and anyone with an exhibition idea — and there are no fees at any stage. The organisation is explicit that it is not a granting body: winning proposals become apexart's own programming. A proposal cannot include specific exhibition dates, cannot itself contain an open call for artists, cannot be a single unified artist project with tasks delegated between contributors, and cannot include sales activity; one proposal per person. The window runs 1–31 October 2026, and the separate international open call for exhibitions anywhere outside New York opens 1 February to 1 March 2027. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 exhibition budget + NYC group exhibition.

item.title: Darkroom Exchange Residencies 2027 · Nordic Analog Network
item.description: The Nordic Analog Network — a programme connecting community photography darkrooms, coordinated by CYAN Studio in Oslo and the Finnish Darkroom Association in Helsinki and supported by Nordic Culture Point — opens its 2027 Darkroom Exchange. Six darkrooms each invite one photographer for an individual residency of roughly three to eight weeks: Mörk in Finland (8 weeks, February–March), Island Darkroom in Scotland (3 weeks, March), Fotoverkstedet in Norway (3 weeks, April–May), CYAN Studio in Norway (3–5 weeks, April–June or August–September), Luovake in Finland (3–5 weeks, August–November) and Björkö Darkroom in Sweden (4 weeks, September). One free application covers all six; you rank your preferred darkrooms in the form and the host darkrooms choose who they invite. Selected artists receive an artist's fee of 15,000 NOK — about €1,400 — rising to 18,000 NOK for those who take a sustainable travel option, and that fee is expected to cover travel and living costs. Accommodation is organised by the inviting darkroom and the workspace is free; some darkrooms also provide chemicals or materials, though special materials are the artist's own cost. Residents work on their own projects alongside the local photographers using the darkroom, and are encouraged to present their work at the host darkroom, with help available to arrange workshops, small shows or artist talks. The 2026–27 cycle carries a theme of sustainable analog photography, but it binds the exchange rather than the work: each resident either attends a workshop on some aspect of it or is asked to teach one for local photographers, and teaching is paid separately as a teacher's fee. The call is open to anyone over 18 living in Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway or Sweden, including the Faroe Islands, Greenland and Åland, working with any analog photographic process — and you must apply to a darkroom in a country other than the one you live in. Applications go through a Tally form with a single PDF containing a short bio, CV, work plan and up to ten images of recent work, at least five of them made with analog processes, in English, named Firstname_Lastname_Open_Call_2026. There is an online meet-up with the 2026 residents and a Q&A about the call on 3 November 2026 at 16:00 CET. Applications close 20 November 2026 at 23:59 GMT, late applications are not reviewed, and invitations go out in the middle of December 2026. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 15,000 NOK artist fee + Residency.

item.title: Experimental Photo Festival 2027 — Exhibition Open Call
item.description: The Experimentalphotofestival Association opens the exhibition call for the eighth Experimental Photo Festival, which runs in Barcelona from 21 to 25 July 2027. Twelve artists or collectives will be selected for twelve solo exhibitions across a programme being built at Centre Cívic Pati Llimona, MUHBA Porta de Mar, BORSÍ pel barri, the Experimental HUB, Mont.BCN and Lab Nau Especial; artists do not apply to a named venue, and the curatorial and production teams assign spaces by the artistic, spatial and technical character of each project. There is no theme. The festival reads experimental photography broadly — analogue, digital, historical, alternative, hybrid and expanded practices, and photography combined with installation, video, sound, sculpture, performance, science or technology — and says applicants need not identify as experimental photographers. Projects may be finished, in progress, or previously exhibited, published or awarded. One €20 application covers three selection routes: the twelve solo exhibitions; a Group Exhibition Mention for a small additional set of artists, whose show stays installed until December 2027 and shares a €600 production budget; and an online feature for twenty artists in Analog Forever Magazine, which the festival says it continues to promote through later exhibitions and screenings. Solo-exhibition artists receive a €150 artist fee paid directly (an invoice is required), a festival-managed production budget of up to €200 that is not cash and covers only pre-agreed expenses, twelve months of access to Ágora's Diploma in Experimental Photography as an in-kind benefit the organiser values at €999, festival access, meals on festival days, merchandise, curatorial and production support and priority — not free — booking at the Col·legi Major Penyafort-Montserrat. Some exhibitions are installed in time for the IPFA Meeting of international festival directors in Barcelona from 30 June to 4 July 2027. Costs sit on the artist's side too: selected artists must be present in Barcelona for installation, opening, the festival and dismantling, are responsible for installing and dismantling their own work with team assistance, and accommodation and travel are not covered. Up to ten project images per application through Picter; each extra project needs its own €20 entry. Entries close 7 November 2026 at 11:59 pm CET and results are emailed in January 2027. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: €20 per project. Prize: €150 artist fee + Solo exhibition (Barcelona) + Publication.

item.title: 0—1 Publication — First Edition
item.description: 0—1, a nomadic curatorial platform based in The Hague that has worked through temporary exhibitions, online publishing and collectible print editions since 2017, is launching a printed edition and inviting contemporary artists into its very first issue. The brief centres on nature without being limited to it, so work that approaches the theme obliquely is as welcome as work that addresses it directly. Only 12 artists will be selected, one image each: the gallery reviews the wider portfolio first and then chooses the final image together with the artist rather than imposing a pick. The edition is produced in a limited run of 100 copies and distributed through 0—1. Each selected artist receives a €50 reproduction fee for the one agreed image; the fee covers this edition only and the artist retains copyright. The call is free to apply to, open to artists at any stage and anywhere in the world, and accepts any medium so long as it can be reproduced as a static image, which includes photography. Existing works only; no new production is expected. Applicants send one link per artist through the gallery's Google Form. Selection is curatorial, the gallery's own terms state it cannot always give individual feedback, and submitting work transfers no copyright. Submissions opened on 10 October 2026, close on 10 January 2027 and results are published on 10 February 2027. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: €50 reproduction fee + Publication (edition of 100).

item.title: 31st Annual NO DEAD ARTISTS International Juried Exhibition · Ferrara Showman Gallery
item.description: Ferrara Showman Gallery on Julia Street in the Arts District of New Orleans is taking submissions for the 31st annual edition of NO DEAD ARTISTS, its international juried exhibition of contemporary art. The gallery tells the show's history on its own call page: Jonathan Ferrara founded it in 1995 "to give a voice to emerging artists", the name coming from "the old adage that artists never achieve success until they are dead" — a notion the show turns on its head, and one it has often made good on by giving emerging artists their first break. It was a New Orleans call in the 1990s, grew to cover Louisiana, became a national juried exhibition in 2010, and in 2014 Matthew Weldon Showman opened it internationally. The gallery says the exhibition has led to national press coverage, gallery representation, art fair exhibition and acquisitions by museums and other prominent collections. Three arts professionals jury each edition — the panel changes every year and the 2027 jury is not yet named, though past jurors include Prospect.1 founder Dan Cameron, New Orleans Museum of Art director Susan Taylor, former Andy Warhol Museum director Eric Shiner, MacArthur Fellow John Scott, Ballroom Marfa co-founder Fairfax Dorn and collector Beth Rudin DeWoody. The grand prize is a solo exhibition at the gallery the following year for one jury-winning artist, which the entry record dates to 2028. Photographers are in on an explicit affirmative rather than on silence: the gallery's own entry record states "Living artists worldwide, at any stage of their careers may apply. All media is accepted." Entries are up to ten artworks — images or video, and detail, installation or contextual shots count toward the ten — for a $40 fee per submission, and the two surfaces disagree on how many bites you get: the gallery's own instructions allot each entrant ten images or videos in total, while the entry record sets a maximum of three submissions per artist, each charged its own $40. Read the money terms before you enter: every submitted work must be available for sale through the exhibition, selected work carries the gallery's standard 50% sales commission, and the artist pays all shipping, including return shipping of unsold work and any import/export duties and taxes. There are no size limits beyond the gallery itself — walls up to 19 feet, ceiling 11.5 feet. Selected work must reach the gallery by 7 September 2027; the show opens to the public on 11 September, has its reception on 2 October during Arts District New Orleans' First Saturday openings, and closes 23 October 2027. — Deadline: June 15, 2027. Fee: $40. Prize: Solo exhibition at Ferrara Showman Gallery.

item.title: Prototyping Futures of Making: Water, Data, and Living Systems · Women Eco Artists Dialog
item.description: WEAD — Women Eco Artists Dialog, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit created in Northern California in 1996 by Jo Hanson, Susan Leibovitz Steinman and Estelle Akamine and still run by a volunteer board — is taking entries for its 2027 member exhibition of ecoart and social justice art. The theme turns the data centre back on itself: at a moment when, as the call puts it, "AI/Data Infrastructures depend on vast quantities of water and land, this exhibition asks what it means to build within systems that are already alive." It wants practices that engage water, data and living systems as sites of construction and consequence — trees transmitting through root and fungal networks, rivers carrying memory and contamination, natural systems registering signals that exceed human language, set against computational systems that abstract, store and intensify those flows. The framing draws on material ecology and interdisciplinary design, naming Neri Oxman's work and Paola Antonelli's curatorial perspective at MoMA, and looks for work that moves past fabrication toward growth, co-production and interspecies collaboration. The jurors say they will prioritise work that closely addresses issues and solutions on this topic. All media are accepted, including sound and video, so photographic and lens-based work is eligible on its own terms. Two jurors: Lisa B. Woods, whose practice moves across art, technology, ecological systems and interdisciplinary research, and Leah Dalton, curator of the physical exhibition at The 109 Gallery in Chickamauga, Georgia. The show runs 1 May to 31 August 2027, online and in the gallery, and comes with a printed catalog, artist presentations on Zoom, a panel discussion, and awards — the organisers say awards will be given but have not published their values. Entry itself is free — one entry per artist, of one to three pieces — but this is a membership show: WEAD states that you must be a paid member to be eligible to be juried, with payment due by the 31 January deadline. The call names a $45 annual fee; WEAD's own membership page prices the basic level at $45 a year and a youth, student and low-income level at $20, says limited scholarships are available on request, and lists the chance to apply to the annual membership shows as a benefit of every level. All women-identified, non-binary and trans-identified artists are invited to join and apply. Works sold through the exhibition carry a 25% commission to WEAD. Entrants pick either online-only or physical-and-online, and anyone taking the physical option pays their own shipping both ways, prepaid return included, plus their own insurance. Work shown in a previous WEAD exhibition is not accepted. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free to enter; WEAD membership required ($45/year, $20 youth/student/low-income). Prize: Exhibition at The 109 Gallery and online + catalogue + awards.

item.title: EFA Studios New Member Application 2027
item.description: The Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts runs one of the few subsidized studio programs left in central Manhattan, and it is open for new members. Up to eighty member-artists hold private studios at 323 West 39th Street, between 8th and 9th Avenues in Midtown Manhattan's Fashion District, in the same building as EFA's Project Space gallery and the Robert Blackburn Printmaking Workshop. A successful applicant gets a private studio for up to two years at below-market cost, with the option to reapply after that; studios run from 200 to 440 square feet with 11-foot ceilings, heat, air conditioning, electricity and shared facilities included, free wired internet, and access 24 hours a day, seven days a week. The money is the thing to read carefully: there is no application fee, but membership is subsidized rent rather than a free residency — fees run from $634 to $2,022 a month depending on the size and shape of the studio assigned and on the artist's demonstrated financial need, plus a monthly due of $80. Budget for the higher end: the complete application guidelines PDF linked from the live form, uploaded at the end of September 2026, prints a higher range of $750 to $2,200 a month for the same studios. That form is also blunt about the odds — EFA accepts between six and nine artists a year and receives 200 to 300 applications a cycle. The studios are not a destination residency and there is no travel or living support — EFA says it welcomes artists living within commuting distance of Manhattan. Eligibility is otherwise broad on medium and narrow on circumstance: visual artists working in all forms of media may apply, but the program is built for artists with a developed studio practice and career, applicants cannot be enrolled in a college or university degree-granting program, and they must be United States citizens or legal U.S. residents for the length of their tenure. The gallery notes that certain work cannot be accommodated for practical reasons — large or heavy sculpture, some metalwork, and anything involving high noise levels. Selection is anonymous and runs in three phases: an Artistic Merit Selection Panel meets in February and reviews each applicant's images projected one by one, judging artistic merit alone, with applicants represented by a number and names withheld; after four or five rounds the panel recommends finalists, who are interviewed between late March and April. Everyone is notified in March, and accepted artists must complete paperwork and take possession of their studios by 1 May. Because the rent is needs-based, finalists are asked at interview stage for two letters of reference — one of them to demonstrate financial responsibility, such as from a landlord — a personal financial statement and full federal tax returns for the last two years filed. The application is free and asks for eight images (or five minutes of video with four images), an image list, a current resume and an explanation of the work in 250 words or less, with no name or identifying links in the text. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free to apply; subsidized membership $634–$2,022/month ($750–$2,200 in the guidelines PDF) plus $80 monthly dues. Prize: Private subsidized studio in Midtown Manhattan for up to two years, with curatorial visits.

item.title: SMALL! 2026 · fortyfivedownstairs
item.description: fortyfivedownstairs — a not-for-profit theatre and gallery established in 2002 by Mary Lou Jelbart and Julian Burnside, on the lower ground floor at 45 Flinders Lane in Melbourne's CBD — is taking entries for the sixth edition of SMALL!, its community-sourced exhibition of small works. The premise is flat and deliberate: every artwork that meets the requirements is hung, nothing is juried out, and all of it is shown anonymously, so visitors choose on the work alone and the artist's name is revealed to the buyer only once a piece sells. Photography is one of the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, prints, textiles and small sculptural work, and there is a dedicated Photography Prize among the nine awards given on closing night — the others being Under 18, Painting, Drawing, Printmaking, Sculpture, Textile, Mixed Media and a People's Choice Award. Prizes are decided by a selection panel of artists, curators and arts workers; the gallery says the values will be confirmed closer to the exhibition and will likely be vouchers from Melbourne art-supply stores in the A$50–A$150 range, so entrants should treat the cash value as unsettled. Everything is priced identically at A$160 regardless of medium or the artist's standing, of which the artist keeps A$125 and the gallery takes A$35 — a commission far below the usual gallery cut. Open to all artists living in Australia with no age restrictions; under-18s can opt into the Under 18 Prize, and the gallery states that discounted entry fees are available to First Nations artists on request. Each artist may enter a maximum of two artworks, one per entry form, at A$25 each, and SMALL! caps the show at 1,000 entries — once the limit is hit the form closes, so the practical deadline can arrive early. Work must not exceed 20 × 20 × 20 cm including any frame or display apparatus and must be ready to hang; unframed works on paper are pinned. Everything entered must be available for sale, and work may be delivered in person or posted; unsold work has to be collected at the gallery across two days in December unless return postage is bought, which costs A$25 added to the entry or A$40 arranged afterwards and is available within Australia only. AI is excluded outright: "Artworks must NOT be created with the use of AI, in any part or form." Entries close 5pm on Monday 9 November 2026, accepted work must reach the gallery by 5pm on Friday 20 November, and the exhibition runs 3–17 December 2026 with a ticketed preview on 2 December, an opening on 3 December and the prize announcement at the closing event on 17 December. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: A$25 per artwork. Prize: Exhibition at fortyfivedownstairs; Photography Prize among nine category prizes.

item.title: Viewings in Black: Image, Object, and the Expanded Frame
item.description: Black Is Magazine — an archival platform launched by photographer Lia J. Latty to spotlight Black photographers and keep a database of everyone it interviews, run single-handedly from Baltimore — is taking submissions for its second print issue. The theme is work that pushes photography past the flat rectangle: assemblage, collage, photomontage, textile and fibre worked into image-based practice, three-dimensional or sculptural uses of the photograph, and work that moves between photography and another medium in a way that expands what an image can do. The call names its lineage — Romare Bearden, Betye Saar, Ralph Arnold, Lorraine O'Grady, Mickalene Thomas — and says it is looking for work in conversation with Black artistic tradition and cultural history, bringing a distinct point of view to identity, memory, diaspora or representation. In the editors' words, it wants work "for whom the image is not the final destination but a starting point, something to be built upon, layered, folded into object, and transformed." Open to emerging artists across the African diaspora regardless of location, where emerging means artists actively developing a practice who have not yet received significant institutional recognition. Submission is free: up to five work samples (JPEG or PNG, minimum 300 dpi for print), an artist statement of up to 300 words, a bio of up to 150 words and a project proposal of up to 250 words explaining how the work connects to the theme. Submission is through a Google Form, selected artists are notified by email, and the magazine states that every submitting artist receives a response. Separately and year-round, the magazine reviews portfolios and books on an ongoing basis for features on the site — 10 to 15 images from one project at 72 dpi and 1000px on the long side, a project statement and a short bio, by email — and says it particularly seeks work by photographers of the African diaspora who are part of the LGBTQIA+ community. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication in print issue.

item.title: SHOTS Magazine #174 — Poems & Prophecies
item.description: Spring 2027 issue (#174) of the black-and-white photography quarterly, independently published since 1986. The theme is POEMS & PROPHECIES, and the magazine asks explicitly for a broad, unusual and creative interpretation — "there is no need to be literal." Submit up to 8 images, grayscale, 300 ppi, minimum 12 inches on the longest side, named Lastname_Firstname_Title. Colour files are converted to greyscale on receipt, so the work has to survive the translation. Submission is free for current and renewing subscribers (up to 8 images); non-subscribers pay $28 for up to 8 images, and either group can add a further 8 images for another $28. Every photographer who submits is mailed a copy of the issue whether or not their work is selected — which is also how you find out: SHOTS sends no notification letters, so the answer arrives with the magazine. Open to photographers internationally, all processes, formats and experience levels. Initial selection is made by editor Elizabeth Flinsch, who then builds a layout and goes over the pairings with publisher Douglas Beasley. The magazine states on the submissions page that all images remain the copyright of the photographer "without exception", and warns readers to be suspicious of contests and publications that ask for ownership. Accepted photographers' city/state/country and website are printed in the back of the issue unless they ask otherwise. Online submission only — SHOTS does not review websites and does not accept unsolicited emailed files. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free for subscribers / $28. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 2028 Solo and Group Exhibition Proposals
item.description: The Rehoboth Art League, an art centre founded in 1938 on a historic homestead campus in Henlopen Acres near Rehoboth Beach on the Delaware coast, is taking proposals for its 2028 season of solo and group exhibitions across four galleries — Corkran, Tubbs, Ventures and Homestead. All mediums are accepted, and the prospectus addresses photography directly in its currency rule: work must have been produced, or for photographs shot, no earlier than 2025, must not have been shown at RAL before, and must be available for the whole run of the exhibition. Solo applicants submit 5 works; groups submit 10, together with an artist statement and a summary CV or bio. Images must be under 4MB with a minimum dimension of 1960px, and only online entries are reviewed. Selected artists get a show in the League's galleries, promotion through its website, social media, printed brochures and press, and keep 65% of anything sold during the exhibition — but note the trailing clause: after the show, 35% is still owed to the League on any work sold to a buyer who first saw it on display during the exhibition. All work must be for sale unless the Exhibitions Director approves an NFS listing, artists pay their own delivery and shipping both ways, and selected artists are expected to attend their opening; housing is not guaranteed but is usually available over opening weekend. Proposals are reviewed by the League's Exhibitions Committee, which says it can accept only a limited number each year; decisions go out on or before 31 August 2027. Artists who showed in the 2025 or 2026 solo/group exhibitions, or who are exhibiting in 2027, are not eligible. Entry is $25 for RAL members and $45 for non-members, non-refundable. NOTE ON TIMING: this is a long-lead call — entries close at 4pm on Monday 26 July 2027, more than nine months out — so it is worth bookmarking rather than rushing. — Deadline: July 26, 2027. Fee: $25 members / $45 non-members. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Translator Issue #5 — Photo Essay
item.description: Translator is a London-founded print magazine that translates and platforms long-form journalism from beyond the Anglosphere — started in 2025, four paper issues published so far, with a core team in London working with contributing editors, translators, writers and publishers worldwide. It commissions one photo essay for each paper edition, and is now pitching for Issue #5. The brief is photographs that explore a social phenomenon or tell a human story, taken by local photographers outside the Anglosphere, ideally with a close personal familiarity with the phenomenon or story the pictures describe; the magazine asks for a unique angle not found in English-language media, locally specific but globally relevant, or something altogether singular to your own media landscape. Translator pays £300–500 and pairs the photographer with an editor to write the text that runs with the images, and the essay is published in print and online. Pitches go to Frankie Jenner, Translator's Managing Editor & Culture Editor, as a short account of the story you want to tell and the angle English-language media has missed, with a preview selection if the pictures already exist and links to previous work. The submissions page the link above reaches also carries a pitch form rather than an address — name, email, a short bio, where you are based and the pitch, with Photo Essay among the format options. Past photo essays have covered Berber and Khartoum in Sudan, the Gen Z protests in Nepal, the gardens of Babur in Afghanistan and Algeria's unfolding eco-crises — and for Issue #5 the editors say they are looking for work from regions they have not yet covered, which is a real constraint worth reading before pitching. There is no submission fee. READING THE PREVIOUS ESSAYS IS NOT FREE, WHATEVER THE CALL SAYS: the Instagram call tells pitchers they can read them online for free by signing up to "our free membership – Language Curious", but the membership ladder on translatormag.co prices Language Curious at £6 a month or £60 a year, and the tier it does mark FREE is Open-Minded, which buys the weekly Overheard newsletter and "free access to a selection of articles on the web" rather than the full archive Language Curious unlocks. Back issues can also be bought in print from the magazine's stockists or through its own shop, which ships worldwide. NOTE ON WHERE THE DEADLINE COMES FROM: the photo-essay commission, the fee band and the brief are all on Translator's own submissions page, which carries no date; the 26 October 2026 close for Issue #5 is published only by the magazine's own Instagram account, @translatormag. The site's own nav lists Issues #1 to #4, which is consistent with #5 being the edition in hand. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £300–500 + publication.

item.title: Digital Explorations 2027 · Maryland Federation of Art
item.description: Maryland Federation of Art's annual exhibition dedicated to digitally-produced art, shown in MFA's Virtual Gallery from 15 February to 14 April 2027. The call is written around what software has done to how artists capture and make work — weaving scenes together in Photoshop, painting through a screen, videos, animations and projections, sculpting with a 3D printer — and names digitally produced photography first among the media it wants, alongside digital painting, illustration, graphic design, digital video and projection; any original 2D or 3D image-based work created or produced through digital software is considered. MFA exhibitions are blind juried, with the artist's name and identifying information hidden from the juror. This edition is selected by Mollye Bendell, an interdisciplinary artist in electronic media and Assistant Professor of Digital Media and Immersive Media Design at the University of Maryland, College Park, who has shown at the Baltimore Museum of Art, the New York Electronic Arts Festival, CURRENTS New Media Festival and the Kennedy Center, and holds grants and residencies from Wave Farm WGXC, Harvestworks and the Tides Institute. Cash awards presented by the juror total $500, announced 1 March 2027 at 5pm. Up to six original works made in the past three years may be entered, uploaded through artcall.org at no more than 10 MB each; video entries go in as a link in the Linked Web Resource field plus a still frame. Work previously exhibited in MFA's Virtual Gallery is not eligible for re-entry, and MFA states plainly that it does not accept work created via image-generative AI. Entry is $45 for one or two works ($30 for MFA members) with up to four more at $6.75 each ($4.50 members); the discount is only for current members, and a non-member who pays the member rate must settle the difference before the deadline or the work is never shown to the juror. Work must be for sale or listed Price on Request, with MFA retaining 20% commission (15% for members) and only artists in the 48 contiguous states able to set a price. TWO ELIGIBILITY SENTENCES SIT IN THE SAME DOCUMENTS: MFA's invitation line — on the call page, in the 2027 prospectus PDF and in the ArtCall FAQ's own answer to "Who is this exhibition open to?" — reads artists residing in any state or territory of the US, Canada or Mexico, while a boilerplate sentence two lines later says entry is open to all artists worldwide bar sanctioned countries. MFA’s own General Guidelines settle it, and they are the document the Terms of Entry bind an entrant to: “Unless otherwise noted, open juried exhibitions are open only to residents of the United States, Puerto Rico, Canada, and Mexico. Online shows are open to artists from around the world, with the exception of sanctioned countries.” This is an online show — the work hangs in MFA’s Virtual Gallery, February 15 to April 14, 2027 — so the international clause governs, and the ArtCall Artist Conditions header agrees: “Entry is open to all artists internationally.” The ordinal is also unsettled: the call page calls this the 7th annual edition, while the 2027 prospectus PDF and the ArtCall listing both still say 5th. Founded in 1963, MFA is a 501(c)(3) non-profit supported by the Maryland State Arts Council and runs Circle Gallery and Avenue Gallery in Annapolis. The 11:59pm deadline is not given a time zone on any surface; MFA is on US Eastern time. — Deadline: December 9, 2026. Fee: $45/2 works ($30 members) + $6.75 each addl. Prize: $500 + exhibition.

item.title: The Unseen — What Lies Beneath the Surface · Artspace Gallery
item.description: A juried exhibition at Artspace, the artist-run 501(c)(3) nonprofit gallery in Richmond's Stratford Hills, inviting artists to explore hidden forces, dreams, memories, spirituality, mystery, imagination and the unseen systems that shape our experience of the world. Open to artists 18 and over in all genres, 2D and 3D, with work made in 2022 or later; photography sits squarely inside this gallery's programme — its own exhibition history carries photography solo shows in the main gallery, and video entries are accepted if the artist supplies the display equipment. Juror Robert Stuart — an MFA painter who moved from representation to abstraction, was selected for the New Orleans Museum of Art Triennial, holds an Academy Award in Art from the American Academy of Arts and Letters and now co-directs Gallery 22 in Staunton — awards $300 and a solo exhibition at Artspace to first place, $200 to second, $100 to third, plus up to three honorable mentions. Entry is 1–3 images with an artist statement for a $35 fee, and Artspace asks anyone for whom that is a hardship to email its exhibition committee for an exemption before submitting. The show runs 22 January – 20 March 2027, opening with an awards reception and a 6:30pm juror talk on 22 January. Accepted work is hand-delivered or shipped to Richmond at the artist's cost with a prepaid return label (plexiglass, not glass), must hang on D-rings and wire, must fit through a 33 × 82¾ inch door, and stays on view for the full run; sales are encouraged but not required, with the gallery retaining 45% commission (25% for Artspace members). The deadline is stated in Mountain Time — 11:59 pm on Friday 4 December 2026 — which is 1:59 am on 5 December for anyone on the US East Coast. — Deadline: December 4, 2026. Fee: $35 (waiver available on request). Prize: $300 / $200 / $100 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Corinne Adams Emerging Artist Fellowship · Atlanta Center for Photography
item.description: Atlanta Center for Photography's fellowship for an Atlanta-based emerging lens-based artist, now in its 2027 cycle. One Fellow is selected by jury to complete and exhibit an individual project over roughly nine months, receiving a $750 artist fee, production and framing support, 1:1 mentorship from Atlanta artist and educator Constance Thalken, professional development, participation in the 2027 ACP Virtual Portfolio Reviews, and a 3-month solo exhibition at the ACP Project Lab on Edgewood Ave opening 20 May 2027. ACP also selects 4–6 artists for the Emerging Artist Fellowship Cohort: monthly concentrated cohort meetings and group critiques, a $325 artist fee, and inclusion in a cohort group exhibition hosted by Day and Night Projects in summer 2027. Open to photography, video art and mixed-media practitioners aged 18+ who live or work in metro Atlanta and are not enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate programme during application or the fellowship. Apply with a 250-word biographical statement and a 350-word exhibition proposal written for the Project Lab's architecture; the $15 fee is paid separately, and ACP asks anyone for whom it is a barrier to email its programme staff. — Deadline: November 3, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $750 artist fee + 3-month solo exhibition.

item.title: Echoes Across Time · Mountain Artists Guild
item.description: The Mountain Artists Guild's winter juried show in Prescott, Arizona is mounted as a concert partnership with the Arizona Philharmonic, whose “Echoes Across Time” programme — Handel's Violin Sonata in D Major, Fazıl Say's Four Cities and Tchaikovsky's Piano Trio in A Minor — is the brief. Artists need not illustrate a particular composition; the brief is what the music awakens — a memory, a place, a person, a culture, a moment in history. The Guild suggests memory and nostalgia, childhood and family tradition, cultural heritage, remembrance, changing landscapes and cities, connections between generations, rhythm and movement, and music translated into colour, shape and texture. Photography is one of the two judged categories in its own right (“all types of photography mediums”), alongside original paintings; the show is 2D only, with no three-dimensional work, and reproductions, giclées and printed merchandise are excluded, as are nudes and work unsuitable for family viewing. CAUTION, TWO CONTRADICTORY ELIGIBILITY LINES ON ONE PAGE: the prospectus header reads “Open to members of Mountain Artists Guild only” and the fee table lists a member rate and nothing else, while a later paragraph reads “this exhibition is open to all artists”; the two sibling shows the Guild ran this year both printed a non-member rate as well, so the members-only reading is the one to plan around. Up to three works may be entered for the base fee, and members also agree to volunteer a minimum of four hours during the run or pay a $20 buyout. Entries are juried for the gallery show and then judged again in the gallery; the juror was still “TBA” when this entry was written. All artwork must be for sale, priced to carry the Guild's 25% member commission, and delivered in person — no shipping — with gallery intake on January 11, 2027. Canvas or frame size must be at least 154 square inches and no more than 1,728. The exhibition runs January 13 to February 14, 2027, award-winning work is shown at the February 14 concert at the Ruth Street Theater, and accepted entries stay in the online Web Gallery for three months. Note the cutoff is not end of day: entries close at 9 PM on January 2, 2027. — Deadline: January 2, 2027. Fee: $30 members only (first 3 works; Guild membership required, price not published). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Create! Magazine Issue #61 — Juried by Deep Space Gallery
item.description: Open call for Issue No. 61 of Create! Magazine, the artist-run print and digital publication, curated for the Winter 2027 issue by Deep Space Gallery in Jersey City. There is no theme this time — all subjects and media are welcome, photography among them — and the call is open to artists worldwide with no academic background required. Every entry goes to the gallery's curators, Jenna Geiger and Keith VanPelt, whose gallery has staged immersive installations at Spring/Break Art Fair during Armory Week, were one of 100 galleries invited into Artsy's inaugural FOUNDATIONS Winter 2024 showcase, and exhibited in PERSONAL STRUCTURES 2024: Beyond Boundaries at the European Cultural Centre during the 60th Venice Biennale. They choose one artist for the cover of the print and digital magazine; the cover artist also gets a feature spread inside the issue, an in-depth feature interview, an invitation onto the Create! Podcast and a free print copy. Additional selected artists receive a four-page spread in the print and digital editions, features across the magazine's website and social channels, and a complimentary digital issue with the option to order print. Submit up to 10 works — cohesive bodies of work and series encouraged — with a 300-word bio and a 300-word artist statement; the standard entry fee of $35 covers three images, with additional fees only if you choose to submit extra images or request an online interview. Artists retain full copyright, and there are no further fees if published. Jurying starts in December 2026, winners are announced in January 2027 and the issue is released in Winter 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $35 / 3 images. Prize: Cover feature + publication.

item.title: Women Street Photographers Annual Exhibition 2027
item.description: The Women Street Photographers annual exhibition, open worldwide to women and non-binary photographers of all ages, with no age gate and no nationality restriction. Seventy finalists are exhibited at El Barrio's Artspace PS109 in New York City from 9 to 19 April 2027 as part of the WSP Festival, and printing and framing for the exhibition are fully covered by the organiser. Leica Camera USA awards four cash grants of US$1,000 each. Selected photographers also get a dedicated profile on the Women Street Photographers website and features across WSP's platforms, which the organiser puts at over 200,000 followers. The jury is Kathy Ryan, for 39 years director of photography at The New York Times Magazine; Sarah Meister, executive director of Aperture and formerly 25 years at MoMA; and Sehin Tewabe, an Ethiopian photographer and co-founder of Artawi Gallery in Addis Ababa. The three of them choose the finalists and WSP founder Gulnara Lyabib Samoilova then curates the hang. Review is blind — each entry is assigned a number and judges see no names or personal details. Entry is single images only, made after 1 September 2020, in street photography, street portraiture or abstract street photography in public spaces anywhere in the world; film, digital and smartphone frames are all accepted, minimum 1500 px on the long side, JPG, sRGB. AI-generated images, multiple exposures, composites, watermarks, text and borders are all barred, as is work previously published on the WSP website. Photographers keep full copyright and WSP takes a non-exclusive right to exhibit and promote selected work. The fee is $15 per photo to a maximum of 25 photos per entry, with a bonus rung — submit 20 or more and five of the entries are free — and anyone wanting to send more than 25 must start a fresh submission. The organiser also offers fee waivers of up to two free entries to photographers who cannot afford the fee (New York City residents excluded) or who cannot pay by card because of US embargo restrictions — request the waiver form by email. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $15/photo. Prize: 4 × $1,000 + exhibition.

item.title: 2026 KinoSaito Annual Community Art Benefit
item.description: KinoSaito's year-end community show, hung salon style in the former St. Patrick's School that houses the arts centre in Verplanck, on the Hudson an hour north of New York City. The open call is free — "There is no application fee to apply, though a suggested donation of $10 per applicant is greatly appreciated" — and the submission guidelines open on "All mediums may be accepted", so a photographic print is eligible on the organiser's own wording. The eligibility gate is physical rather than curatorial: accepted artists must transport their own work to KinoSaito and collect it again if it does not sell, so the organiser states that only artists within commuting distance of 115 7th Street, Verplanck, NY 10596 are eligible to submit. Artists at any stage of their careers are encouraged to apply, and the organiser frames the show as a way of highlighting the talent in its own community as the centre heads into a sixth year of operation. The page says each artist may submit up to two works and that a maximum of one will be selected, but the application form marks both image uploads as required, so have two pieces ready. Work must be ready to hang or display, no larger than 36 inches in any direction, and priced at no more than $3,000 — and it must be for sale, with the artist keeping 50% of the sale price and the other 50% going to KinoSaito as a donation from the artist. The exhibition runs 11–20 December 2026, with an opening reception and performance on 12 December from 4 to 7 pm. Artists are notified on 29 November; drop-off is 5, 6 and 7 December and pick-up 20, 21 and 22 December. KinoSaito's programmes are supported by the New York State Council on the Arts and ArtsWestchester. — Deadline: November 11, 2026. Fee: Free (suggested $10 donation). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Keyhole · Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo
item.description: A themed group show at Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo in Lakewood, Colorado, built on a single image: "What do you see when you look through the keyhole? Maybe it's a secret room, a forbidden world, a memory, a dream, a hidden self, or a future waiting to be discovered. Perhaps the keyhole represents curiosity, privacy, desire, access, exclusion, transformation, or the tension between what is revealed and what remains unseen." The gallery describes itself as a lowbrow/outsider contemporary art gallery in the 40West Arts District, on the art walk circuit and in the same shopping centre as Casa Bonita, with good foot traffic on First Fridays. 2D and 3D work is accepted at $30 per piece, up to two pieces per artist. Photographic work is eligible as a printed, properly framed or mounted object — the gallery will not display digital artwork unless it is printed and framed or mounted properly, and will not accept photographic work that depicts another artist's artwork, including street art, without that artist's express permission. Everything must arrive ready to hang, meaning hanging hardware already attached: hanging wire is preferred, no adhesive mounts, and work that is not ready to hang will be rejected at drop-off. All work must be for sale with 40% of any sale going to the gallery, and cannot be sold elsewhere for the run of the show. Copyright stays with the artist. Drop-off is 30 January 2027, the First Friday reception is 5 February 2027 from 6 to 9 pm, the show runs to 26 February and pick-up is 27 February. Out-of-state artists are responsible for shipping both ways. — Deadline: January 9, 2027. Fee: $30 per piece. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Big Sky · Webster Arts
item.description: A national call for art opening Webster Arts' 2027 gallery season in Webster Groves, Missouri: "Every sky can be big. Webster Arts invites submissions for our opening show of 2027, Big Sky — artists may submit 2D and 3D artwork that delves into the sights that stir our souls. From vast, natural geographies to constructed architectural skylines, whether mapping the terrains of our souls or the layouts of our living rooms, you are invited to explore the expanses of your world." Work should be original and completed within the last three years. The medium rule is an explicit affirmative with one exclusion — "The exhibit will consider artworks of all mediums except for video" — so photography is admitted by the rule rather than by silence. An independent juror selects the exhibition and two cash awards: $250 Best in Show and one $100 Award of Excellence. This is an in-person exhibition on view 8 January to 8 February 2027, with an opening reception on Friday 8 January at 6:30 pm; accepted work must be shipped to or dropped off at the gallery by 23 December 2026 and stay for the full run. Framed wall pieces must be wired and no larger than 48 x 48 inches, all wall works on paper must be framed, and three-dimensional work must not exceed 32 x 32 x 60 inches or 50 pounds. No reproductions, and work previously exhibited in any Webster Arts gallery is not eligible. Sales are encouraged, and Webster Arts retains a 30% commission on all gallery sales, with local sales tax charged on top and handled by the gallery. Webster Arts has run exhibits, workshops, a plein air event, an art fair and concerts for over twenty years. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: $25 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $250 + $100.

item.title: Cabin Fever 2027 · Cape Fear Studios
item.description: Cape Fear Studios' midwinter show in its Main Gallery in downtown Fayetteville, on display 22 January to 23 February 2027, with an opening reception and awards on 22 January from 6 to 8 pm. The prospectus is explicit on both counts that matter: "This is a non-juried exhibition and is open to all artists, 18 or older" and "MEDIA: All media accepted." Each artist may submit up to two original works completed in the last two years; work must not be copied from another artist or from published material, and must not have been previously exhibited in Cumberland County. Awards are cash — First Place $125 and two Honorable Mentions of $50 each — presented at the opening reception. 2D work may not exceed 40 x 40 inches including the frame and must be properly wired with picture wire and D rings or eye hooks (no saw-tooth hangers); 3D work must be ready to display and free of quality issues not integral to the piece. All entries must be for sale at the price listed on the entry form, no work may be withdrawn early, and the studio retains 30% commission on sales, with payment to the artist within 30 days of the close of the exhibit. ENTRY IS HAND-DELIVERED ONLY, in person at the gallery on 14, 15, 16 and 19 January 2027 — "No late entries will be accepted" — which in practice makes this a call for artists within reach of Fayetteville. — Deadline: January 19, 2027. Fee: $15 (1 piece) / $25 (2 pieces). Prize: $125 / $50 x2 + Exhibition.

item.title: Paradise After-Hours — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
item.description: A public art exhibition on billboard ad space in New York City, curated by photographer Olivia "LIT LIV" Morgan and opening 11 December 2026: "A call for artists documenting queer nightlife and queer art." SaveArtSpace frames the brief against a real pressure — "For years, queer nightlife has faced pressure from city and government offices to shut down the bars, dance halls, and clubs that serve as safe spaces for queer people to dance, perform, and be fully themselves. Venues close. The community keeps creating." The call invites artists who are documenting and preserving that world as it shifts and changes, and asks for work that shows the best of the community: "the joy of the dance floor, the bright lights, the feeling of being free and being seen. The culture the mainstream now borrows from was born in queer spaces like these. They can try to close our spaces, but we have always existed and we always will." Artists of all ages and talents may submit between 8 October and 2 November 2026. Selected work is placed on a billboard in New York, NY from 11 December 2026 and stays up for at least one month; the selected artist is announced after 16 November 2026. Fees go to producing the exhibition, including buying the billboard space, and are tax-deductible donations to SaveArtSpace, a 501(c)(3) non-profit founded in 2015 that works to put culture over commercialism in urban advertising space. The entry form is the binding prospectus and it settles three things the call page does not: media — "All art is accepted. Media NOT accepted: Corporate logos, personal advertising and videos. Please submit still jpegs only", so photography is eligible by the organiser's own enumeration; the real cap of ten images, at a maximum 2 MB each; and the closing clock time of 11:59pm on 2 November. The form also charges the stated donation plus card fees, so the amount actually taken at checkout is $36.92 for one to three images, rising to $108.45 for ten. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Billboard exhibition in New York City.

item.title: Winter Solstice 2026 — Annual Members Exhibition · Griffin Museum of Photography
item.description: The Griffin Museum's annual Winter Solstice members' exhibition fills the Main Gallery in Winchester, Massachusetts with unframed prints from the museum's membership — "a chance to gather the many perspectives of our community into a single, radiant show, and to send a little bit of art home with new collectors before the year closes." Last year the museum made room for over 300 prints, hung wall to wall, and it is asking its members to fill the gallery again. The show is deliberately built to be collectible rather than competitive: each member submits one unframed photographic print, no larger than 13 inches on the longest side, ready to hang with clips or pins or to sit on a pedestal, with a maximum price point of $250 — "We want to give you an opportunity to find a collector for your print, so that you make some holiday money, and a small portion is donated to the museum to support our end of year giving." Submissions open 1 October and run through the month of October; registration comes first, prints are shipped from 1 November and must reach the museum by 1 December. The exhibition opens 11 December 2026 with an artist reception on 12 December, and closes 10 January 2027, when print sales are finalised and payments made. Membership of the Griffin Museum is required to submit; the museum's own membership ladder prices Individual at $70 a year, Students & Educators at $35, Senior (65+) at $50 and Distance Member — which requires residence outside the New England states — at $50, with Family at $100. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free (Griffin membership required: $70/year, $50 outside New England, $35 student). Prize: Exhibition + print sales.

item.title: Thresholds · A Photographer's Place
item.description: A monthly juried show in Gallery X at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, built around the threshold as "a place of passage: a boundary between one state and another, between arrival and departure, certainty and possibility. It is not simply a line that separates, but a space in which transformation can occur." The gallery asks photographers to consider the places, experiences and moments that exist between states of being — transition and liminality between interior and exterior, presence and absence, intimacy and distance, memory and experience, the known and the unknown. The threshold may be architectural or psychological, personal or collective, tangible or imagined; it may be marked by a dramatic event or exist in the quietest of gestures — a pause before leaving, a landscape at dusk, a body in transition, a familiar place rendered unfamiliar. Work that embraces ambiguity and resists easy definitions is explicitly welcomed, as are photographs that reveal thresholds, question them, cross them or linger within them. Selected work hangs in Gallery X at the front of the space from 6 November to 1 December 2026, with an opening reception on 6 November, and is then presented on the gallery's website to be viewed year-round. Up to 5 JPEGs, colour or black and white, minimum 3000 pixels on the longest side. Accepted artists may optionally have their work printed by the gallery on its Canon imagePROGRAF PRO-1100. — Deadline: October 22, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 5 images). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Open Theme: 2026 · Black Box Gallery
item.description: An open-themed juried group photo show at Black Box Gallery in Portland, Oregon: "Open to all themes and ideas, all styles and genres, all perspectives on crafsmanship and photographic creativity." The gallery names landscape, architecture, portraiture, documentary, fashion, still life, conceptual projects, street, colour and black and white, nature and night photography as all welcome. Juror Todd Johnson, the gallery's founder and director, selects 26 photographs for the physical show (1–25 December 2026), with a further 50 for the online gallery annex; all 76 are reproduced in a catalog available on Blurb Books. Black Box provides free printing, matting and framing for every selected work — archival inkjet on Epson Premium Luster in a colour-calibrated environment, presented in 18"x24" black frames with pre-cut white mats. Selected photographers supply a high-resolution TIFF or JPEG; the gallery prints one exhibition print only, and no sale or further printing happens without the photographer's prior consent. Exhibition prints are kept in the gallery flat files for two years to promote the photographer to collectors, curators and critics, then shredded. Entry is by email with a PayPal fee payment: up to 5 JPEGs, 1200 pixels on the longest side at 72 PPI, 5 MB or less each. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. The gallery takes 50% commission on sales, and work does not have to be offered for sale. — Deadline: November 13, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 5 photos). Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Seasons 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: International photography exhibition on the seasons, running at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 4 to 28 March 2027. "Seasons come and go, but each season can have its own distinct look and feel" — from the greens of Spring to the blues and whites of Winter, the gallery says the palette of each season changes and in turn changes how we see the world around us, and it wants photography that highlights those distinct changes and how they affect the environment around us. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi, 3000 pixels minimum on the shortest side) by free file transfer — Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox — to the gallery's submissions address; attachments are discouraged because they compress the files, and all images should be sent together. Selected work is printed and displayed in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the gallery's website, and included in an exhibition catalogue. Selected participants also receive a digital certificate of participation before the exhibition opens, have their installed work photographed and filmed for the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers who are selected pay a £50 participation fee covering printing and installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image, and a discount is available to anyone selected for both March exhibitions. Acceptance notification is by 4 November 2026 and the payment deadline for selected photographers is 18 November 2026. Only selected photographers are notified. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Women in Photography 2027 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Open-themed international photography exhibition for women photographers, running at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography from 4 to 28 March 2027. The gallery has marked International Women's Day for several years with a show of work by women photographers from across the globe, and says this year is no different: "Women in Photography is an open-themed exhibition, meaning any theme or genre of photography is accepted", so there is no subject brief to answer — only the work. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi, 3000 pixels minimum on the shortest side) by free file transfer — Smash, WeTransfer or Dropbox — to the gallery's submissions address; attachments are discouraged because they compress the files, and all images should be sent together. Selected work is printed and displayed in the gallery, shown in an online gallery on the gallery's website, and included in an exhibition catalogue. Selected participants also receive a digital certificate of participation before the exhibition opens, have their installed work photographed and filmed for the gallery's social media, and are automatically put forward for Photographer of the Month. Submission is free; photographers who are selected pay a £50 participation fee covering printing and installation, with prints presented in gallery-owned frames at 16"x12", 18"x12" or 12"x12" depending on the image, and a discount is available to anyone selected for both March exhibitions. Acceptance notification is by 4 November 2026 and the payment deadline for selected photographers is 18 November 2026. Only selected photographers are notified. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free (£50 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Protest, Everything's Connected · Photobook Cafe & Rapid Eye Darkroom
item.description: The eighth quarterly open call from Photobook Cafe and Rapid Eye Darkrooms, in partnership with UNCLE, takes protest as its theme — "visible in the streets, in our homes, online, in landscapes, within communities and in the everyday choices we make", loud or quiet, collective or deeply personal. The call asks how photography can document, challenge and reimagine acts of resistance, solidarity and social change, and it is explicit about the range it wants: climate and environmental action, social justice and equality, anti-war and peace movements, Indigenous rights, feminist, LGBTQIA+ or disability rights activism, or any other movement advocating for change. Documentary, conceptual work, portraiture, landscape, still life, archival material and experimental image-making are all named as welcome, and the organisers say they particularly want work that moves beyond protest-as-event — the people behind movements, the spaces they occupy, the lasting effects of activism, the quieter forms of protest that go unseen. Work may be new or drawn from personal archives, analogue, digital or alternative process, taken anywhere in the world. Guest judges Rebecca Zephyr Thomas (who has photographed LGBTQ+ activists for Dazed and Ukrainian protesters for Elephant, and worked with the Green Party and Extinction Rebellion) and Jade Smith (a director, photographer and filmmaker whose practice centres on protest, community and social documentary) select 35 exhibiting photographers for a group show and zine launch at The Photobook UK Gallery on 11 November 2026, with Best in Show announced that evening at 19:30. Of the 35, ten receive a 30-minute one-to-one mentoring session on portfolio development, project direction and professional practice; three Best in Show photographers are invited into a Photobook UK Public Programme group exhibition in 2027 with select printing supported by Rapid Eye Darkrooms; and ten have their work shown in an UNCLE street gallery across London, taking the work out of the gallery and into the public realm. Each of the 35 finalists receives a complimentary copy of the group zine featuring all 35 selected photographers, along with an exhibition print of their selected image, per the organiser's press release. £25 covers one to ten images and you may submit as many times as you like at that rate; the organisers state that if selected there are no additional costs to exhibit, that all exhibition prints are produced by Rapid Eye Darkrooms on digital C-Type matte or gloss paper, and that the call is not-for-profit — a portion of fees goes to Not A Phase and Just Stop Oil, chosen by the judges, with the rest reinvested in the free photobook collection, the gallery programme and youth engagement. Eligibility is stated as wide open: emerging, established or amateur, any age, background and identity, from anywhere in the world. Entry is two steps and the form enforces the order: pay the £25 on the organiser's Squarespace store, then upload your images to the Google Form together with a screenshot of the payment receipt, which is a required field. Files are JPG at 2400px on the long edge, 300dpi, RGB, named forename_surname_photograph title_No., and selected photographers may be asked for a higher-resolution file for printing. Note on access: the gallery has no step-free access and is reached by 25 steps. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: £25/10 images. Prize: Exhibition + zine publication.

item.title: Open Call for 2028 Exhibitions · Open Source Gallery
item.description: Open Source Gallery, a W.A.G.E.-certified 501(c)(3) in a renovated carriage house on 17th Street in Brooklyn, is choosing its 2028 exhibition programme by open call, and the terms are unusually good for a $15 application. The gallery invites proposals from “artists working in any medium and location, whose practices emphasize experimentation, sustainability, and social engagement” — photography is eligible, and the application form asks for Artistic Medium as free text rather than a pick-one list, so there is no medium gate. Selected artists receive artist fees calculated on the W.A.G.E. certification schedule, a production budget, and support from the gallery in planning, production and communications; this is a funded, produced exhibition rather than a wall rental.
