THE FEE IS WAIVABLE AND THE CALL PAGE IS THE ONE SURFACE THAT DOES NOT SAY SO: both the application form and the payment screen add “Open Source Gallery is a nonprofit art gallery, and our programs are always free or pay-what-you-can. The $15 Open Call fee is a donation that helps us continue to offer this programming. If the fee is cost-prohibitive for you, please email us… and we will work out an accommodation”, while the call page on the gallery's own site carries no waiver sentence at all. The $15 is paid through a dedicated donation link whose only preset amount is labelled “$15 (Required Application Fee)” — its single alternative is a box for increasing the figure, so $15 is a floor and not a range — with PayPal for applicants outside the US, and the payment confirmation is uploaded with the application. One PDF carries everything: a project proposal of no more than 1,000 words, an artist statement of no more than 250 words, a CV, and 10 to 15 images of recent work. The gallery shows conceptually-driven work from local and international artists on a monthly rotation alongside public programmes, and publishes its floor plan so proposals can be made to the actual room at 306 17th Street. Applicants will be notified in early 2027. No juror is named. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Exhibition + W.A.G.E. artist fee + production budget.

item.title: The Contemporary Print 2027 · PrintAustin
item.description: PrintAustin's 14th annual juried international exhibition, held with The Art Galleries at Austin Community College. READ THE MEDIUM RULE BEFORE YOU PAY: this is a printmaking survey and straight photography is excluded — “Solely digital and photographic prints are not eligible” — but photopolymer plate is one of the six techniques the organiser names as eligible, in its own words “lithography, relief, intaglio, silkscreen, photopolymer plate (i.e. SolarPlates), and monotype”, and “while non-traditional or digital output is accepted as a print element, submissions must utilize traditional print media as their primary technique.” So a photographer working in SolarPlate or photopolymer photogravure, or using a photographic element inside a work whose primary technique is printmaking, is eligible; a photographer submitting an inkjet or darkroom print is not. Any 2-D or 3-D work qualifies if printmaking is the sole or primary technique, including ceramics, sculpture, mixed media and artist books, and unless it is an installation nothing may exceed 72 inches in any direction. The jury is blind and the juror is Lauren Rosenblum, the Jensen Bryan Curator at The Print Center in Philadelphia, who has organised more than a dozen exhibitions there and previously held curatorial positions at the Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. THERE IS A FEE LADDER AND A WAIVER, NOT A SINGLE PRICE: $35 for three pieces, $10 instead of $35 for PrintAustin members, $10 for each additional piece over three up to six, and the organiser states “We have a limited number of waived registration fees regardless of membership status for artists in need should you be experiencing hardship”, available by email. Best in Show takes $500 in cash plus a podcast interview by Hello, Print Friend, in English or Spanish. TWO BARS SIT ONLY ON THE CaFE PROSPECTUS AND BIND ANYWAY: works shown in a past Contemporary Print may not be re-entered, and “Artists that were accepted into our 2025 The Contemporary Print are also ineligible--please join us in 2027!” — so a 2025 acceptee pays $35 for nothing. Work is consigned at a 70/30 split in the artist's favour, with PrintAustin responsible for safekeeping and insuring the work while it holds it and payment due within five weeks of a sale. Shipping is the artist's to arrange, the artist carries transit risk in both directions and must enclose a prepaid return label or the work will not be hung — but it is not unsubsidised: “Selected artists will receive a shipping stipend, courtesy of PrintAustin. Stipend amount minimum will be $50, exact amount TBD.” THE DELIVERY DATE IS NOT SETTLED ON ITS OWN RECORD: the terms say “by December 9, 2026”, the shipping block says only “in December”, and the organiser's own IMPORTANT DATES table says “JAN 9 Artwork due”; PrintAustin tells applicants to “Refer to direct correspondence from PrintAustin for updated info.” The exhibition runs at The Art Galleries at Austin Community College, 6101 Highland Campus Drive, with a reception on 27 February 2027. PrintAustin Collective is an artist-led nonprofit that runs an annual printmaking festival in Austin from 15 January to 15 February. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 ($10 PrintAustin members; hardship waivers available). Prize: $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: Geographies: An Exploration of Places, Environments and Cultures · LoosenArt
item.description: LoosenArt's third open call running concurrently on its calls page, and the one it labels outright a “Call for Publication and Exhibition”. The brief asks what the places we inhabit and move through tell us today, and how landscapes, environments and cultures change the way we perceive boundaries: the publication will bring together works examining the relationships between the physical and the symbolic, human presence and the environment, and local experience and global processes, so that geographical, cultural, political and emotional boundaries become starting points for exploring territories, belonging and transformation through personal perspectives. ENTRY IS FREE AND THE CALL IS WORLDWIDE, and photography heads the organiser's own list of accepted media: “Photography, video, digital, visual design, visual data, installation, sculpture, painting.” Each artist may submit one to three works. The guaranteed outcome is publication — the works are selected for a new issue of the Issue Collective editorial project dedicated to this theme. The exhibition is a second, conditional stage: “Some of the works selected for publication will also be considered in a further selection for the LoosenArt Collective #2 exhibition, planned for 2027 in Milan, Rome or Cagliari, Italy” — the organiser has not fixed which city. Submission is through a single Google Form that LoosenArt shares across all of its live calls; a required “Select the call of interest” dropdown assigns the entry, and this call appears there as “Geographies - An Exploration Between Places, Environments and Cultures”, alongside Aesthetic Dynamics, Revelations and the closed Homo Technologicus. The form asks for name and surname, country, email, website, Instagram, how you heard about the opportunity, an artist statement of up to 70 words in English, and for each of up to three works a title, year of realisation, a file of no more than 5 MB, and a URL for video only. Files go out through SwissTransfer to the organiser's submissions address rather than uploading into the form. LoosenArt is a spare Google Sites presence whose contacts page names Antonio Muratore at an address in Quartu Sant'Elena, Sardinia; beyond the call text it publishes no further terms, and no charge of any kind is mentioned at any stage, on the call page or in the form. — Deadline: December 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: The Big Small Show 2026 · Drawing Rooms
item.description: Drawing Rooms closes its 25th anniversary year with The Big Small Show in what the gallery calls its eleventh year, a survey of work made in the past two years, hung across the nonprofit's expanded galleries — The Terrarium Gallery and The Alcove Gallery — inside the Mana Contemporary complex in Jersey City from 10 December 2026 to 17 January 2027. This is not a theme show: the organisers say outright “Is there a theme? No, just send work you would like to be considered, and the curator will identify and create groups/connections of concepts”, and the hang is built as a “curatorially-driven narrative” in which works “connect and interact with each other visually and conceptually”. ANY MEDIUM IS ACCEPTED AND PHOTOGRAPHY IS NAMED IN THE LIST: “painting or drawing on paper, canvas, or other media; sculpture, collage or textiles, photography or prints”. Small is preferred but not mandatory — work dropped off in Jersey City can be any size, while anything shipped must be no larger than 18 x 24 inches and travel flat in a rigid mailer or tube with return postage included. Prints may come unframed, framed or mounted on a cradled panel; if framed, the organisers ask for simple white, black or wood-tone frames no more than five inches larger than the image, and no floating acrylic. Entry is $35 for up to three images and there is no cash award: what comes back is the exhibition itself, a written curator's statement, a review, inclusion in the Artsy.net presentation and the organisers' newsletter and social channels, and consideration for Drawing Rooms' other programmes including The Art Project JC lobbies and its online Artsy exhibits through the year. ALL WORK MUST BE FOR SALE, with sales split 60% to the artist and 40% to Drawing Rooms, paid out within 30 days of the gallery receiving payment; work is insured from the moment it is in the gallery's possession. Whatever the gallery picks for Artsy stays listed there at the same 60/40 split for up to two months after the show closes, and entering commits the artist in advance to a collector discount of up to 10%, with the curator asking approval for anything deeper, to 20%. Notifications go out on 5 November 2026, hand delivery runs 20–22 November at Drawing Rooms and The Oakman, and mailed work must arrive by 23 November. AI is excluded: “Works must be original. No AI or reproductions of original works.” Drawing Rooms is a project of Victory Hall Inc., a 501(c)(3) running exhibitions, programmes and public art in the NJ/NY area since 2001, supported by the New Jersey State Council on the Arts. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Portrayed 5: A Juried National Exhibition of Portraits · d'Art Center
item.description: The fifth edition of d'Art Center's portrait show takes over the 2,200 sq ft Main Gallery of the Norfolk nonprofit, in the heart of the city's NEON arts district, from 9 January to 6 February 2027. The brief is narrow in subject and wide open in treatment: work must depict a human figure or a human face, and the organisers list Realism, Traditional, Abstract, Modern, Impressionist, Pop Art, Cubism, Surrealism, Contemporary and Street among the styles they want, “all styles of portraiture are welcome”. The call is national, all-medium and explicitly “open to all functional, non-functional, 2D, 3D, fine art, and fine art craft in ALL STYLES”, so photographic portraiture competes on the same wall as painting and sculpture; d'Art runs photography-specific shows in its Vault space in other months, so the medium is part of the programme rather than a loophole. Entry is $35 for three submissions — three images is the minimum, so one strong piece can be entered with detail shots or repeated — and each further work is $5 to a cap of ten. Gallery Director Amanda Bradley curates alongside a guest juror still to be named, and that juror picks the awards: $500, $300 and $150, paid by cheque within 45 days of the reception. Entrants must be 18 or older and living in the United States, work must have been made in the last eight years without the aid of an instructor or kit, weigh under 50 pounds and measure no more than 60 inches in its longest dimension, though Bradley can waive the size and weight limits by prior arrangement. Notifications go out by 5pm on 23 November 2026 and accepted work must reach Norfolk by 5pm on 19 December. Sales split 60/40 in the artist's favour, meaning a 40% gallery commission; artists pay shipping both ways and must include a prepaid FedEx or UPS return label (no USPS, no freight, no packing peanuts). The exhibition is also archived permanently on d'Art's online archive site, and the 14 January reception is streamed. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 works), $5 each additional. Prize: $500 / $300 / $150 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Deets: A National Exhibition of Intricate and Heavily Detailed Artworks · d'Art Center
item.description: d'Art Center fills The Vault — a historical bank vault inside the Norfolk nonprofit's building, kept as a small, close-up exhibition space — with “the art of meticulousness” from 9 January to 6 February 2027. The call wants work that rewards standing still: “artworks that emphasize intricate detail, layered complexity, and exquisite finesse”, from elaborate craftsmanship and subtle nuance to “unexpected elements revealed upon closer inspection”, so that visitors “slow down, look closer, and appreciate the artistry found in every mark, texture, and thoughtfully considered detail”. No medium is excluded and the eligibility text says only that “all styles and aesthetics are considered”; the scale of the room sets the real limit, with work capped at 36 inches in its longest dimension, a cap the Gallery Director can waive by prior arrangement depending on how much of the installation the artist takes on. For a photographer this is a show for the dense frame — fine-grain large-format detail, alternative-process surfaces, collage and hand-worked prints — rather than the single clean gesture. Entry is $30 for three submissions, three images being the minimum, with each further work $5 to a cap of ten. Gallery Director Amanda Bradley curates, and the awards are chosen by a panel of d'Art Center's own professional artists and staff: Best in Show takes $300. Entrants must be 18 or older and living in the United States, and work must have been made in the last eight years without the aid of an instructor or kit, and arrive hang- or pedestal-ready. Notifications go out by 5pm on 23 November 2026 and accepted work must reach Norfolk by 5pm on 19 December. Sales split 60/40 in the artist's favour, meaning a 40% gallery commission, and work may also be marked NFS; artists pay shipping both ways and must include a prepaid FedEx or UPS return label (no USPS, no freight, no packing peanuts). The reception on 14 January is shared with Portrayed in the main gallery, and the show is archived permanently online. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $30 (3 works), $5 each additional. Prize: $300 Best in Show + Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Programme 2027 — Open Call · Foto Forum
item.description: Open call for the 2027 exhibition programme of Foto Forum in Bolzano — the South Tyrolean photography society's own gallery at Weggensteinstraße 3F, open Tuesday to Saturday with free admission, running exhibitions, photobook presentations, talks and workshops. The call is for a real exhibition slot, not a group hang: “Foto forum welcomes submissions from photographers, visual artists and other personalities working with photography”, and the organiser lists Exhibitions, Workshops and Talks/conferences as three separate submission categories with only Exhibitions carrying this deadline. NO THEME IS SET and no genre is excluded. WHAT AN EXHIBITION PROPOSAL MUST CONTAIN, verbatim from the guidelines: “8-20 images of the project (JPG)”, “Video links, if the project contains moving image work”, “Abstract of the project (PDF)”, “CV (PDF)”, “Installation proposal for our spaces (PDF)” and a “List of existing works, material, measures etc (PDF)” — so this wants a finished, installable body of work and a plan for the room, not single images. THERE IS NO ENTRY FEE: the guidelines enumerate the submission in full and never mention payment, and submission is by email to [email in contacts.json], with the organiser asking for “non-expiring file transfers with sharabke link that allows us to directly see hi-res images” and, if using Dropbox, a shared link rather than a folder invitation. NOTE THE ORGANISER'S OWN CUTOFF IS AMBIGUOUS: the page reads “Exhibitions (deadline 15th October 2026, midnight 00:00 am)”, and midnight 00:00 is the start of the 15th rather than its end, so treat 14 October as the safe date. No juror is named and no notification date is published. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Breakthrough ’27: A Sioux Falls Emerging Artist Showcase · Washington Pavilion Visual Arts Center
item.description: Free, no-jury showcase for emerging artists in the Everist Gallery at the Visual Arts Center inside the Washington Pavilion, Sioux Falls — eight galleries and South Dakota's largest art museum. Presented by Sioux Falls Stage & Gallery, which “invites emerging Sioux Falls-area artists to submit work for Breakthrough ’27: A Sioux Falls Emerging Artist Showcase, on view Dec. 18, 2026–March 28, 2027.” PHOTOGRAPHY IS NAMED, not implied: “all artistic mediums are welcome, including drawing, painting, sculpture, ceramics, photography, digital art and more.” THERE IS NO ENTRY FEE AND THERE IS NO SELECTION STEP — the museum states “there is no cost to participate, and all eligible artwork that meets the submission and content guidelines will be accepted while space remains available,” so the only competitive element is the awards. CASH AWARDS, presented at the Sioux Falls Stage & Gallery event and artist reception on Feb. 18: Best in Show $500, Breakthrough $200, Sioux Falls Spirit $200 — $900 in total, a figure summed here from the three the museum lists; no total is advertised. FOUR BINDING BARS: the artist must live within a 10-mile radius of Sioux Falls city limits; must never have had a solo exhibition at the Visual Arts Center; submits exactly one artwork; and that work must be no larger than 50 × 50 inches, no heavier than 75 pounds, and delivered ready to install. SUBMISSION IS IN PERSON ONLY — “artwork must be submitted in person. Online submissions will not be accepted.” Work and a completed paper form go to the Visual Arts Center front desk on the second floor on one of three Fridays: Oct. 23, Nov. 13 or Nov. 27, each 10 a.m.–4 p.m., with Nov. 27 marked “final opportunity.” NOTE THE CUTOFF IS 4 P.M., NOT MIDNIGHT. CONTENT GUIDELINES BIND because the show is open to visitors of all ages: work “must be appropriate for a general audience, including young children” and “should avoid explicit nudity or sexual content, graphic violence or disturbing imagery, profanity or overtly mature themes and overly political or religious content.” The museum publishes no AI policy for this call. — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $900 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 2028 Solo Artist Application · The Art League
item.description: Application for a 2028 solo exhibition at The Art League gallery at 105 North Union Street in Alexandria, Virginia — inside the Torpedo Factory Art Center, and described by the gallery itself as "one of Washington's largest art galleries". THE GALLERY NAMES PHOTOGRAPHY EXPLICITLY in its media policy, which is the test worth checking before paying anything: "Photography: unique photographed images are acceptable. Photographers are encouraged, but not required, to process or print their own work. Unaltered reproductions of pre-existing artwork are not allowed (i.e., you may not take a photograph of a painting — yours or not — and submit it as an original)." WHAT THEY WANT: "artists who have a strong, cohesive, and exciting body of work expressing an aesthetic concept", and the stated aim, "whether we exhibit experimental or traditional works, is to adhere to the highest standards of quality. While we seek beautifully executed work, we also value work that is innovative, artwork that presents the artist's unique voice and engages the viewer intellectually, emotionally, and visually." THREE STAGES: five artwork images plus a detailed proposal, an artist statement and a résumé are submitted online; jurors review the applications and pick a group of finalists; the finalists physically drop off the same five works for in-person jurying, which happens without the artists present. APPLICATIONS RUN TWO YEARS AHEAD — this round is juried in November 2026 for shows in 2028. THREE ELIGIBILITY BARS, ALL BINDING: the artist must be a current Exhibiting Artist member of The Art League; the artist cannot have had a solo exhibit at The Art League in the last five years; and if selected, no more than one third of the works in the final show may have been shown in a juried solo exhibition within 50 miles of the gallery. COSTS: $50 to apply through Submittable, plus Exhibiting Artist membership at $115 for a new member or $105 on renewal — free for artists aged 23 and under under the gallery's Emerging Artist tier. NOTE WHAT THE ALL-INCLUSIVE MEMBERSHIP DOES NOT COVER: the $182 all-inclusive programme "covers Exhibiting Artist dues and all entry fees for exhibits held in the exhibiting year with the exception of solo exhibits, some specialty exhibits, and Gallery 75 fees", so the $50 is payable whichever membership you hold. AI GENERATED WORK IS NOT ACCEPTED, stated on the gallery's own media policy: "AI generated artwork is not accepted at this time." The 2028 jury panel is listed as "Jury Panel TBA" on the application itself. The gallery publishes its evaluation criteria in full — concept, the clarity of the statement, the detail of the proposal, cohesiveness of the body of work, technical skill and craftsmanship, professional presentation, and the formal elements — but on its own Solo Artist Jurying page, which has not been updated past the 2027 cycle, so read the criteria as the gallery’s standing ones and take every date and juror name from the application. Deadline Sunday 1 November 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $50 (Exhibiting Artist membership required, $115 new / $105 renewal; free for artists 23 and under). Prize: Solo exhibition in 2028.

item.title: Open Call AIR Lebensbogen 2027 — Industrieviertel · Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich
item.description: Free open call, no entry fee, for the Lebensbogen artist-in-residence programme in Grünbach am Schneeberg, Lower Austria, run by Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich with the Lebensbogen institution. ALL DISCIPLINES ON THE CALL, SEVEN NAMED ON THE DETAIL SHEET: the call block says the programme "lädt Künstlerinnen und Künstler aller Kunstsparten zu einem Arbeitsaufenthalt" — artists of every art form are invited to a working stay — while the linked detail PDF narrows that to a list, "Eingeladen sind Personen aus den Bereichen Bildende Kunst, Baukultur, Film, Musik, Literatur, Digitale Medien und Darstellende Kunst." Photography is named on neither surface and excluded on neither; it sits inside Bildende Kunst and Digitale Medien, and the CV asked for must carry a portrait photograph. WHAT THEY WANT: "künstlerische Vorhaben, die sich mit dem Ort, seiner Geschichte, der Natur oder den Lebensrealitäten der Menschen vor Ort auseinandersetzen" — projects engaging the place, its history, its nature or the lived realities of the people there, with "Begegnungen auf Augenhöhe" (encounters as equals) with residents and staff at the centre and a traceable place in the artist's own practice. Participatory and inclusive formats are expressly welcome. Lebensbogen's Christof Mikats frames it as space rather than a commission: "Kunst braucht Freiraum – um Neues auszuprobieren, verrückte Dinge zu machen und manchmal ganz neue Wege zu gehen." WHAT THE PROGRAMME COVERS: free accommodation, free board, use of available work and event rooms, introductions to the regional arts scene, the possibility of a closing presentation, and possible remuneration for participatory or inclusive formats ("mögliche Vergütung partizipativer oder inklusiver Formate" — possible, not guaranteed). WHAT THE ARTIST PAYS: travel to and from the residency and all working materials, stated plainly as "selbstständige Finanzierung von An- und Abreise sowie Arbeitsmaterialien". WHAT THE HOST IS, AND IT IS THE THING TO KNOW BEFORE APPLYING: the Lebensbogen is not a village studio but a residential and working community for people with disabilities and mental illness — "Der Lebensbogen bietet Menschen mit Behinderungen und psychischen Erkrankungen einen Lebensplatz, der Wohnen und Arbeiten miteinander verbindet." Participatory projects are welcome but expressly not therapeutic ("Partizipative, jedoch nicht therapeutische Projekte"), those are the ones that may carry a fee, and experience of artistic work with people with mental or physical impairments is stated as an advantage. 2027 is the pilot year; individuals or collectives may apply; the stay is in a fully equipped living container beside the workshop hall or a unit in the new residents’ centre, on an eight-hectare former mining and industrial site with hangars and a large workshop hall that projects may use. Residents are also required to attend a meeting day on site — attendance is "Voraussetzung für die Aufnahme in die finale Auswahlrunde", the precondition for reaching the final selection round — to engage with the site and the people there, and to leave behind a work or a documentation. STAY: 3 to 12 weeks, scheduled between April and October 2027; applicants state their preferred window and length. TWO ELIGIBILITY GATES, BOTH BINDING: artists and craftspeople with a connection to Lower Austria ("mit Niederösterreichbezug"), and membership of Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich, which is "für die Einreichung Voraussetzung" — a precondition for submitting, not merely for the stay. THE MEMBERSHIP IS CHEAP AND OPEN, NOT JURIED: the association publishes its "JÄHRLICHER MITGLIEDSBEITRAG" as €25 for "Künstler:innen/ Einzelpersonen" (€50 for associations, institutions and groups, €100 for businesses, €160 for municipalities), applied for through an online form, effective on payment and cancellable in writing each year. Submission is one PDF of at most 8 MB with a CV carrying a portrait photograph, a portfolio, a short description of the project and the requested dates, sent by email to the Industrieviertel office. Deadline Tuesday 1 December 2026. No notification date is published on either surface. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free (Kulturvernetzung NÖ membership required, €25/year individual). Prize: Free 3–12 week residency + accommodation and board.

item.title: In Character · L.A. Photo Curator
item.description: Open call from L.A. Photo Curator on character, identity and presence — "photographs that reveal personality, identity, presence, and the many ways people inhabit the world." The brief is deliberately wide: "A character study can focus on someone else — or on yourself. It may be direct or subtle, staged or spontaneous. Character can emerge through a face, a gesture, clothing, posture, surroundings, relationships, or the small details that tell us something about a person." The curator is explicit that the sitter need not be fully visible: "The subject does not have to look directly at the camera, or even be fully seen." Juried by Laurie Freitag, who founded the platform eleven years ago. EVERY ENTRANT IS SHOWN: "All entrants included in the online group exhibition (with artist statement, bio, and website)". First place receives a solo online exhibition, an online article including a Q&A with the juror's responses, and their image on the L.A. Photo Curator splash page for one month; selected work is also considered for Top 40 Images of the Year and the Photographer of the Year title. ONE UNUSUAL RETURN: "One participating photographer will be invited to serve as a Guest Juror alongside Laurie Freitag for a future L.A. Photo Curator competition." Entry is $25 for either three or six images — exactly those numbers, not "up to" — paid by PayPal or card through the page's Buy Now button, then emailed as a ZIP of JPEGs at 1024 pixels on the longest side, 72 DPI, under 1 MB each. A limited number of fee waivers are available on request. Five per cent of entry fees goes to Best Friends Animal Society and another five per cent to a charity the winner chooses. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. Deadline November 1, 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Solo online exhibition.

item.title: Open Call M-ZONE 2027 — Weinviertel · Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich
item.description: Free open call, no entry fee, for two curated exhibitions in the M-ZONE — a roughly 150 m² hall in Mistelbach, Lower Austria, that sits between two of the region's major institutions, the nitsch museum and MAMUZ. 2027 starts a new cooperation between Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich, the nitsch museum, MAMUZ and the Province of Lower Austria, and the two shows it produces are what this call fills. WHAT THEY ARE LOOKING FOR: "künstlerische und kuratorische Konzepte, die aktuelle Fragen aufgreifen und eine eigenständige Haltung entwickeln" — artistic and curatorial concepts that take up current questions and develop a position of their own. The organisers ask for projects that treat the hall as more than wall space: "Willkommen sind Projekte, die die M-ZONE nicht nur als Ausstellungsfläche verstehen, sondern den Raum in ihre inhaltliche und formale Entwicklung einbeziehen" — projects that draw the room itself into their conceptual and formal development. New and existing projects both qualify, the existing ones "adaptiert oder weiterentwickelt" for this space. NO MEDIUM IS NAMED AND NONE IS EXCLUDED: the call asks for exhibition concepts rather than a medium, so a photographic project with a spatial idea competes on the same terms as any other — but equally, photography is not singled out as welcome, and an applicant is pitching a show, not submitting images. WHO CAN APPLY: "Einzelpersonen, Kollektive & kuratorische Teams mit Niederösterreichbezug (z.B. Wohnort, Arbeitsort)" — individuals, collectives and curatorial teams with a Lower Austria connection, residence or workplace given as the examples. No membership in Kulturvernetzung is required for this call, unlike two of the organiser's other current open calls. WHAT A SELECTED PROJECT GETS: a four-week exhibition and a total project budget of €3,000. The venue's own page describes the space as "rund 150 m² Raum für Kultur, Kreativität und Feste – mit moderner Infrastruktur". HOW IT IS JUDGED: "Die Auswahl erfolgt durch eine Fachjury aus Vertreterinnen und Vertretern der beteiligten Institutionen sowie externen Jurymitgliedern" — a specialist jury of representatives of the participating institutions plus external members, assessing "künstlerische Qualität | räumliche und konzeptionelle Schlüssigkeit" (artistic quality, spatial and conceptual coherence). No juror is named. WHAT TO SEND, in one PDF of at most 8 MB, by email only: the exhibition concept including images, portfolios and CVs of everyone involved, and contact details with an email address and phone number. TIMELINE: entries close Monday 2 November 2026, the jury sits in November 2026, results are announced in January 2027, and the two exhibitions run March/April and July/August 2027 with exact dates still to be set. The whole call is published in German. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €3,000 project budget + four-week exhibition.

item.title: Come In! Galerie Waidhofen/Ybbs — Open Call 2027 · Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich
item.description: Free open call, no entry fee, for six multi-week solo exhibitions in 2027 at the Come In! Galerie — a roughly 30 m² exhibition room in the Impulsquartier in Waidhofen an der Ybbs run specifically for artists under 29, by Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich as part of the province's Come On! youth-culture programme. THE OFFER IS PAID, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT UNUSUAL FOR AN AGE-LIMITED FIRST-SHOW CALL: a fee of €500 and up to €500 in material-cost reimbursement ("Honorar € 500 und bis zu € 500 Materialkostenersatz"), support for the exhibition and the opening, optional guidance on exhibition design and installation from experienced curators ("Auf Wunsch Begleitung bei der Ausstellungsgestaltung und beim Aufbau durch erfahrene Kuratorinnen"), inclusion in an annual publication that collects the year's shows, and introductions to the regional art scene. WHO IT IS FOR, in the gallery's own second person: "Du bist zwischen 14 und 29 Jahre alt und stehst am Beginn Deiner künstlerischen Laufbahn" — aged 14 to 29 and at the start of your artistic career — plus "einen persönlichen, künstlerischen oder beruflichen Bezug zu Niederösterreich", a personal, artistic or professional connection to Lower Austria. No membership is required. ONE CONDITION WORTH READING BEFORE APPLYING: you must be present in person at the gallery during opening hours on the first weekend of your exhibition (Friday 16:00–19:00, Saturday 10:00–13:00, Sunday 15:00–18:00), so this is not a send-and-forget show. NO MEDIUM IS NAMED, in either direction: the call asks for "Deine Werke" and a "Werkübersicht für die geplante Ausstellung (Fotos oder Links)", so a photographic body of work is as admissible as any other, but photography is not singled out as welcome. HOW IT IS JUDGED: "Die Bewerbungen werden von einer Fachjury beurteilt" — a specialist jury, its six members named not in the call block but on the gallery's own page at kulturvernetzung.at/de/come-in-galerie/ — selecting six artists on "künstlerische Qualität, Motivation, Potenzial und Engagement in Hinblick auf die Realisierbarkeit einer Ausstellung" (artistic quality, motivation, potential, and commitment measured against whether the exhibition can actually be realised). WHAT TO SEND, by email: a portfolio or work overview for the exhibition you are planning (photos or links), a CV focused on your artistic work so far, and an artist statement saying why you want to exhibit and what inspires you. THE 2027 SLOTS ARE ALREADY DATED: 19 February–14 March, 2–25 April, 21 May–13 June, 3–26 September, 1–24 October, and 12 November–5 December 2027. The call is published in German, and receipt of an application is confirmed. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 + up to €500 materials + Publication.

item.title: Fresh Eyes Gallery — Call for Submissions · ViewPoint Gallery
item.description: Rolling, free call for the Fresh Eyes series at ViewPoint Gallery, a photographer-run fine-art photography gallery founded in 2000 on the Bedford Highway in Halifax Regional Municipality, Nova Scotia. FRESH EYES IS A MONTHLY SLOT, NOT A GROUP SHOW: "Fresh Eyes is a monthly exhibition series at ViewPoint Gallery designed to showcase the work of Maritime photographers", and the space is a defined 5' × 5' wall — "You get to decide how you would like to make use of it." That is small, and it is the whole point: one photographer at a time, with the layout left to them. NO FEE AND NO COMMISSION, which is unusual enough to state plainly: "There is no fee to exhibit and, in the event of sales, the Gallery does not charge commission" — the only deduction is a 10% handling charge on credit or debit sales. WHAT THE GALLERY DOES: "We'll take care of printing your wall cards and artist statement/bio", and "Your show will be highlighted on our website and social media". WHAT THE ARTIST DOES: "All works should be printed and prepared for hanging by the artist." WHO CAN APPLY: "All artists must be from Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, or New Brunswick" — the three Maritime provinces, and nowhere else. WHAT TO SEND, by email with "Exhibition Chair" in the subject line: an artist statement about you as a photographer, a statement of exhibition intent saying what you intend to exhibit and why, a very brief bio, and 2–3 digital images. All images must meet the gallery's published content guidelines, which sit on their own page. THERE IS NO DEADLINE AND NO ANNOUNCED CYCLE — the call is open-ended, which is why it is listed as continuous; the gallery's separate guest-exhibition route asks for submissions at least three months ahead of an opening, so planning that far out is the gallery's habit. ONE THING TO SEPARATE THIS FROM THE GALLERY'S OTHER DOOR: ViewPoint's solo guest exhibitions in the main gallery carry a $150 non-refundable exhibition fee plus shipping and catering at the artist's expense. Fresh Eyes does not. Note also that the gallery states it cannot insure work on display. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Monthly solo exhibition slot, no sales commission.

item.title: ContemporaryIdentities Issue #31
item.description: Free open call for the 31st issue of ContemporaryIdentities, "an independent quarterly international online magazine covering contemporary art from around the world" whose stated focus is "to showcase and promote experimental and progressive contemporary art through short art reviews from international scholars, art writers and art critics". Selected artworks are featured in the next issue alongside the magazine's invited criticism and artist interviews. THE MEDIA DOOR IS WIDE OPEN AND SAID SO: "Visual artists in any disciplines are welcome to submit artworks in any medium for our 31st Issue" — photography is not singled out but it is not excluded by any medium restriction either, and the call carries no theme. WHO RUNS IT: editors-in-chief and founders Sara Berti and Dr. Elham Shafaei, with a curatorial board of Dr. Izmer Ahmad and Dr. Zoltán Somhegyi; the magazine states it has been chosen for the Arts and Society database, in partnership with the Conseil International de la Philosophie et des Sciences Humaines (CIPSH), UNESCO-MOST, The Global Chinese Art, Culture and Society (GCACS) and Mémoire de l'Avenir. WHAT TO SEND: three to five high-resolution images with each work's title, year, medium and size, plus an artist statement and a short bio, by email. ONE WARNING THE MAGAZINE GIVES ITSELF: "We are not able to respond to each individual. We will only contact the successful applicant" — so silence after the deadline is the expected outcome for everyone not selected, not a lost email. Applicants must be 18 or over. The cutoff is stated in the magazine's own timezone, UTC+04:00, which runs ahead of European and American clocks — a European entrant effectively loses the last part of 15 October. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.
